raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary
- Set `GroupedLinear` split alignment from the active recipe: 1 for BF16/FP16 and Blackwell FP8 current scaling, 16 for Hopper FP8 current scaling, and 128 for MXFP8/NVFP4/FP8 block scaling. An explicit value applies unless the deprecated environment override forces 256.
- Reject negative splits at every alignment and check 16-byte uniform and discrete-A GEMM leading dimensions, with or without bias.

## Cause
PR #3745 passed the default `split_alignment=128` into the device-side scan for every grouped-tensor path. Unquantized BF16 accepts 32-row groups, so `TestFuser.test_deferred_param_init` trapped at the forward call. Passing alignment 1 alone also bypassed the scan's negative-size guard; this PR makes that guard unconditional.

## Validation
Built and imported exact PR head `565bb89a` on H100 NVL and GB200 PyTorch containers. No new test was added, per request.

| GPU | Focused grouped-linear deferred-init | Full `test_fusible_ops.py` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 NVL | 2 passed, 12 deselected | 1,773 passed, 1,859 skipped, 0 failed |
| GB200 | 2 passed, 12 deselected | 2,395 passed, 3,661 skipped, 0 failed |

Command: `PYTHONPATH="$TE_PATH" python3 -m pytest -q tests/pytorch/test_fusible_ops.py --tb=short --disable-warnings`.

A separate GPU process on each architecture using splits `[-1, 65]` and `split_alignment=1` reached the device-side negative-size error and failed as expected.

Summary

`GroupedLinear` now chooses split alignment from the active recipe and GPU. - GroupedLinear picks split alignment from the active compute recipe. - Split scans reject negative sizes at every alignment. - Grouped GEMM checks that matrix dimensions span 16 bytes. No new actionable issues were found. Review checks were static; no build or GPU tests were run. Reviews (7) · Last reviewed commit: ["Check discrete grouped GEMM input alignm..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/1f4810511ce49e585a04519b5a4f46a0744bde97) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Negative splits bypass checks** Passing `split_alignment=1` also removes the check for negative split sizes. The scan checks `split < 0` only inside `if (args.split_alignment > 1)`. An unquantized call with splits such as `[-1, 65]` now passes negative offsets and invalid dimensions to native GEMM instead of rejecting them. Keep the device-side nonnegative check unconditional and skip only the divisibility check.

nodes.body:
Making the contract different for quantized and unquantized compute is hacky and unintuitive. If the user has promised a certain alignment, we should expect them to provide it.
```suggestion
        quantized compute.
```

Instead of making the contract more complicated, I see two alternative solutions:
1. Change the default from 128 to `None`. In that case, we just check for the recipe's minimum alignment.
2. Relax the alignment check when the user-promised alignment is stricter than necessary (https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/pull/3785/changes#r4427584832).

1 is more logical, but it might increase the scope of this PR.

nodes.body: **Duplicate declarations break the build** The added block declares `split` and `invalid` again in the same scope, after their declarations at lines 92 and 94. This prevents `splits_to_offsets.cu` from compiling and blocks the common library build. Remove the duplicate block and keep the synchronization after `block_scan[tid] = split`.

**FP8 backward accepts unsupported splits** `_default_split_alignment` now allows any split size for FP8 current scaling, but Hopper still needs splits divisible by 16 when computing weight gradients. For example, splits `[1, 127]` with 128-wide features pass forward checks. In backward, `layout="NT"` selects physically transposed columnwise data, so each split becomes the FP8 leading dimension. The new feature-width check does not check that dimension, so backward sends unsupported dimensions to cuBLAS and can fail. Keep a 16-element split requirement for this path, or pad the columnwise data and its layouts. **Knowledge Base Used:** [Native GEMM and quantization kernels](https://app.greptile.com/nvidia-public-github/-/custom-context/knowledge-base/nvidia/transformerengine/-/docs/native-gemm-and-quantization.md)
